get.description: Public liveness endpoint; operational topology and queue details stay private.
Operators only (read). Hiding a reported listing is an operator write and is not built yet (R-052).

post.description: Operators only: undo a removal. The asset is exactly as before; the upheld reports stay on record.

get.description: Operators only. Includes the reporter, because the operator has to be able to follow up.

post.description:
Operators only. ``restore`` rejects the report; the hold is lifted once no other report on the asset is open.
``remove`` upholds it; the asset stays hidden for everyone (nothing is erased).

get.description: `AIS_API.ops.customers({from,to,group_by,by})`: per bucket and key: signups, churned, active_end, trials, converted (+ totals, coverage).
One row per company (company = workspace id; names and e-mail addresses live with the identity provider). `from`/`to` select by joining time.
Cohorts by joining month: how many companies had NOT churned n months after joining. A cell exists only when the cohort is at least n months old.

put.description:
Operator: set plan (a text slot, no amounts) / contract dates / status. A churn status (ended, cancelled) records ``churned_at`` (now, kept on later
edits) and the reason; going back to trial/active clears it. Every changed field is written to the append-only history with the operator's id.

get.description:
Deletion requests with their grace deadline, so the operator sees what is waiting and what is due. Nothing is deleted here: the purge
itself stays the documented manual procedure (scripts/purge_requests.py with an explicit confirmation). The free-text reason is not shown.
The newest package downloads (who took what, when, how big) of every workspace: the download audit trail (R-035).
Deep health (database, storage, disk, workers, backup); 503 when any check fails. Platform operators only.
The limits in force and how often they refused someone (counts only; no names).
Read-only integration readiness; restricted to platform operators.

post.description:
Store a validated source image for the independent Photo Engine workflow.

The rights fields are recorded in the asset provenance and, when confirmed, in upload_rights_confirmations (D2).
``rights_confirmed=true`` is required unless ASSET_REQUIRE_RIGHTS_CONFIRMATION is explicitly switched off (L-04).

get.description: Check private stored bytes against upload-time size and SHA-256 metadata.
D2: whether the uploader confirmed the rights to this image. Assets uploaded before enforcement read as unconfirmed.
The hold on an asset, for people allowed to see the asset. Carries no reporter or report text.

post.description:
New version of an asset. A new version of an IMAGE asset is a new photo, so it needs the same rights declaration as
POST /v1/assets/images (D2); 3D model versions are unaffected.

get.description: Stream an immutable AssetVersion only while the caller remains a workspace member.
Return the identity validated by the configured authentication provider.

post.description:
File a report. The answer is the same whether or not the asset exists or the report changed anything, so the
endpoint cannot be used to find out which asset ids exist.

get.description: Public: the document versions a user must accept. ``status`` stays ``draft`` until the texts are final.

post.description: Copy a published item into the caller's workspace as an ordinary asset (editor role or higher). The item itself is never changed.

get.description: Short-lived signed link (like the asset preview links): usable by an tag, valid for the item's current version only. The picture is a downscaled screen copy (long edge at most LIBRARY_PREVIEW_MAX_EDGE), never the original file.
Public listings of every seller. Payloads are never in a search result.

delete.description: Takes the listing out (kept as a record for open reports; nothing is erased).

post.description: Makes it public. The seller confirms the rights again at this moment (recorded: who, when).
The answer is the same whether or not the listing exists or the report changed anything (no probing for listing ids).

get.description: The caller's id and the workspaces they belong to (with their role). No name or e-mail: the server does not know them.
Optional consents (default: not granted). Separate from accepting the terms and privacy policy.

put.description: Grant or withdraw an optional consent. History is kept; withdrawal takes effect immediately.

post.description: Record a deletion request. Nothing is deleted here; an operator processes pending requests.

get.description: Assets of the caller that are on hold, with the state. No reporter and no report text.

post.description:
Owner only, and only while collection is switched on. ``acq`` is written ONCE (a second call keeps the first: first touch is the fact);
``survey`` can be updated. Neither carries an IP address, an e-mail address or a name.

Upload a file straight into the library: images carry the same rights/likeness declaration as every image upload (L-04, recorded in
asset_provenance); a 3D item must be a .glb/.gltf (validated, external references refused).
File an EXISTING asset of this workspace (an upload, a photo result, a generated output) under a kind.

get.description: For building filters: every attribute key in use (optionally within one kind) with its values and how many items carry each.

post.description:
R-060: file a FINISHED job's result under ``render``. Idempotent: the same result is filed once (a repeat returns the existing item with 200).
The server records ``service``, ``style``, ``region`` and ``source_asset_ids`` (the inputs it knows about plus the caller's extra ones, which must be
live assets of THIS workspace); the caller may add other attributes (e.g. ``sku``). Generation-job results must be approved first (R-046).

delete.description:
Takes the item out of the library. The asset stays in the workspace unless delete_asset=true, which goes through the normal asset
deletion (so references from products/characters and generated-output retention still block it).

get.description: R-049: counts read from the 3D file's own JSON (meshes, triangles, materials, textures, animations ...) for the library and the viewer.

put.description:
R-049: the picture shown for a 3D item. The server has no GPU renderer, so the browser's 3D viewer renders it and uploads the result
(a small PNG/JPEG/WebP, at most 1024 px and 2 MB). Replacing it removes the previous one. Only 3D items have a thumbnail (other kinds ARE images).

delete.description: Removes the draft and every candidate that was not chosen (the chosen picture belongs to the brand model and the library).

get.description: For each asset id: the status of its LATEST review ('none' when it never had one) and whether it may be exported (latest review approved).

patch.description: Owner or admin only. Every change of a value is written to an append-only history.

delete.description: Removes the job record and its output picture file (deletion keeps the normal asset rules, so a still-referenced output stays).

post.description:
The built-in mock makes a video inside the request, so a job is never waiting or running: it is always finished (succeeded or failed) and there is nothing to cancel.
The answer says so (409); a real provider's queued job will become cancellable when one is connected.
Runs a FAILED job again with the same pictures and settings as a NEW job (the failed one stays as a record). Counts toward the same limits as any new video.

get.description: Newest change first. ``archived=true`` lists the archived items INSTEAD of the active ones.

delete.description: Nothing is deleted: the item is archived (hidden from the list; ``restore`` brings it back).
